title: Solving |x - 3| + |x + 1| = 6 by Case Analysis
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Solve the absolute value equation |x - 3| + |x + 1| = 6 over the reals by splitting the number line into regions determined by the critical points of the moduli.

steps.title: Locate the Critical Points and Split the Line
steps.explanation: Each modulus changes its internal sign at its zero, so the three regions separated by -1 and 3 are where the equation has three different linear faces.
steps.why: The definition |t| = t for t >= 0 and |t| = -t for t < 0 is piecewise, so removing the bars legally requires region-by-region work.

steps.title: Solve the Left Region
steps.explanation: Below -1 both x - 3 and x + 1 are negative, so both bars flip signs; the resulting equation gives x = -2, which indeed lies in the region.
steps.why: A candidate is accepted only after verification against the region's own inequality; -2 < -1 passes.

steps.title: Show the Middle Region is Empty
steps.explanation: Between the critical points the x terms cancel to the constant 4, so the sum of moduli never reaches 6 anywhere in the middle region.
steps.why: Geometrically, 4 is the distance between the two marker points 3 and -1: any point between them has exactly that total distance, a floor the equation demands be exceeded.

steps.title: Solve the Right Region
steps.explanation: Above 3 both quantities inside the bars are positive, so the bars drop unchanged; the solution x = 4 satisfies x > 3 and is accepted.
steps.why: Again the region check validates the candidate: 4 > 3, so it is a genuine solution of the original equation.
